vo_text: On Mercury, the sun's closest planet, why does water ice survive four hundred and thirty-degree heat?
markers: Frame 0 rotating Mercury + 01 / 08 MERCURY progress strip

vo_text: The ice hides in polar craters that never see sunlight.
markers: Immediate answer < 12 s: Prokofiev polar craters in permanent shadow

vo_text: At fifty-eight million kilometers out, sunlight shines up to seven times brighter than on Earth, yet without an atmosphere to retain heat, you would feel night plunge to minus one hundred and eighty degrees Celsius.
markers: 58M km / 7x sunlight -> split +430 C day -> real terminator -> split -180 C night (DATA #1)

vo_text: In 1965, Italian mathematician Giuseppe Colombo solved its spin mystery.
markers: WHO #1: Giuseppe Colombo (1920-1984) — Italian mathematician · WHEN: 1965

vo_text: Mercury rotates on its axis three times, once every fifty-nine Earth days for every two eighty-eight-day orbits. So one solar day lasts one hundred and seventy-six Earth days, just over two Mercury years.
markers: DATA #1b: 3:2 spin-orbit dial (59d spin, 88d orbit -> 176d solar day)

vo_text: With a radius of two thousand four hundred and forty kilometers, a blueberry beside an Earth nickel, Mercury is the second-densest planet because a metallic core fills about eighty-five percent of its radius.
markers: Real Mercury limb -> DATA #1c + SCALE: 2,440 km (blueberry vs nickel), 85% metallic core · FACT #1: Second densest planet

vo_text: With almost no axial tilt, deep polar craters stay in permanent shadow, where MESSENGER, orbiting Mercury from March 2011 to April 2015, verified water ice inside Prokofiev Crater. Why is Venus hotter?
markers: Edit label: 'Almost no tilt' (0.034 deg) · WHEN: Mar 2011-Apr 2015

vo_text: At one hundred and eight million kilometers out orbits Venus, nearly Earth's twin in size. What would you see dropping beneath its sulfuric acid clouds?
markers: REPAIRED (zero PIA00271): Real Mariner 10 PIA23791 right globe -> Pioneer Venus UV pvo_uv_790205

vo_text: You reach the hottest planetary surface in our solar system. A runaway greenhouse under a ninety-six point five percent carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat and bakes the rock to four hundred and sixty-four degrees Celsius. Surface air crushes at ninety-two bars, like nine hundred and thirty meters underwater on Earth.
markers: DATA #2 + SCALE: 464 C, 92 bars (930 m underwater), 96.5% CO2 · FACT #2: Hottest planetary surface

vo_text: However, Venus spins backwards every two hundred and forty-three Earth days while orbiting in two hundred and twenty-five days, so the sun rises in the west.
markers: REQUIRED R11 PIA00215 real Magellan SAR (118.05-124.40 s) -> Venus backwards spin graphic (124.40-130.75 s)

vo_text: In 1978, Pioneer Venus found deuterium at one hundred times Earth's ratio, evidence that Venus once held much more water. On the 1st of March 1982, Soviet lander Venera 13 survived one hundred and twenty-seven minutes, nearly four times its thirty-two-minute design.
markers: PIA23791 right globe -> Venera 13 panorama · WHEN: 1978 & 1 Mar 1982

vo_text: At one hundred and fifty million kilometers, one astronomical unit orbits Earth, the largest rocky planet. What secret shields our oceans? Tilted twenty-three point four degrees, Earth spins every twenty-four hours.
markers: Real DSCOVR EPIC rotating Earth + NASA/NOAA Suomi NPP Blue Marble 2012 (PIA18033)

vo_text: At the equator, the surface moves at about one thousand six hundred and seventy kilometers per hour, more than four times the four hundred and eight kilometer per hour gust measured during Cyclone Olivia. Rotation makes Earth forty-three kilometers wider across the equator than pole to pole.
markers: DATA #3a + SCALE: 1,670 km/h equatorial spin (>4x Cyclone Olivia), 43 km bulge

vo_text: Some three thousand kilometers beneath our feet, below the rocky mantle, begins Earth's swirling liquid iron outer core, generating a magnetic shield that flipped one hundred and eighty-three times in eighty-three million years.
markers: ORBIT ACTS (027 shelf Omni) -> DATA #3b: 3,000 km outer core · 183 reversals in 83M years

vo_text: German mathematician Carl Friedrich Gauss introduced absolute magnetic intensity measurements in the 1830s.
markers: WHO #2: Carl Friedrich Gauss (1777-1855) — German mathematician · WHEN: 1830s

vo_text: Over the past two centuries, ESA reported in 2020 a roughly nine percent global average weakening, yet our atmosphere shields us from radiation like thirteen feet of concrete. Why did Mars freeze?
markers: WHEN: 2020 (ESA ~9% weakening) · SCALE: 13 feet of concrete atmosphere shield

vo_text: At two hundred and twenty-eight million kilometers, one point five astronomical units orbits Mars, about half Earth's width. Why did its river valleys freeze into a robot desert? Mars has no global magnetic field today, though its crust preserves traces from four billion years ago.
markers: Real Mars globe + Curiosity Gale Crater · WHEN: 4 billion years ago

vo_text: Its thin atmosphere has a mean surface pressure of six point three six millibars, under one percent of Earth's, and an average temperature of minus fifty-nine degrees Celsius.
markers: DATA #4a: 6.36 mbar (<1% Earth) & -59 C mean · NUMBER OBJECT (Ch 4)

vo_text: Mars also hosts the solar system's largest volcano, Olympus Mons, reaching twenty-one point three kilometers above Mars' zero elevation datum, over twice Mount Everest across an Arizona-sized base.
markers: Real Viking & MGS Olympus Mons -> DATA #4b + SCALE: 21.3 km above datum (>2x Everest, Arizona-sized base)

vo_text: After a global dust storm silenced solar-powered Opportunity on the 10th of June 2018, exceeding its ninety-Martian-day design life by sixty times, NASA's Ingenuity helicopter completed seventy-two flights in that thin air through the 18th of January 2024. What looms beyond the asteroid belt?
markers: WHEN: 10 Jun 2018 (Opportunity 60x design life) & 18 Jan 2024 (Ingenuity 72 flights)

vo_text: Holding nearly three hundred and eighteen Earth masses, more than twice the mass of all the other planets combined, it spans eleven times wider than Earth, a basketball beside a grape. However, Jupiter has the shortest day of any planet, spinning in nine point nine hours on a twelve Earth year orbit.
markers: DATA #5a + SCALE: 11x wider (basketball vs grape), 318 Earth masses, 9.9-hour day

vo_text: At 1.4 billion kilometers, 9.5 astronomical units orbits Saturn.
markers: Real Cassini backlit ring mosaic & Saturn globe

vo_text: Nine times wider than Earth, a volleyball beside a nickel, Saturn spins in 10.7 hours at 687 kilograms per cubic meter, the only planet less dense than water. Its ring system extends up to 282,000 kilometers from the planet, yet the main rings stand about 10 meters thick.
markers: DATA #6a + FACT #3: Less dense (687 vs Water 1,000 kg/m3), 282,000 km radial rings (~10 m thick)

vo_text: Why are they vanishing? During 2017 dives between the innermost D ring and cloud tops, Cassini measured ring material pouring into Saturn at 4,800 to 45,000 kilograms per second, while six gravity crossings weighed them at 0.41 Mimas masses, indicating they may have formed 10 to 100 million years ago.
markers: WHEN: 2017 Cassini dives (4,800-45,000 kg/s inflow, 0.41 Mimas mass, 10-100 Myr possible age)

vo_text: Then at Saturn's North Pole spins a six-sided jet stream noticed by Voyager in the early 1980s, 30,000 kilometers wide, wider than two Earths.
markers: Real Cassini north-pole hexagon & central eyewall · WHEN: early 1980s

vo_text: Its 322-kilometer-per-hour winds circle a central hurricane eye, while the region inside the hexagon changed from blue to gold between 2012 and 2016, possibly because of seasonal haze.

vo_text: Found on the 13th of March 1781 by British astronomer William Herschel as the first telescope planet, Uranus is four times wider than Earth, a softball beside a nickel, on an 84-Earth-year orbit.
markers: WHO #4: William Herschel (1738-1822) — British astronomer · WHEN: 13 Mar 1781 · SCALE: Softball vs nickel

vo_text: Why are its seasons so extreme? While Earth tilts 23.4 degrees, Uranus tips 97.77 degrees, more than four times Earth's tilt, possibly from an ancient collision rolling sideways and spinning backwards every 17 hours to plunge each pole into a 21-year winter.

vo_text: Voyager 2 made the only visit on the 24th of January 1986.

vo_text: Because Uranus drifted off course, French mathematician Urbain Le Verrier calculated an unseen planet's position for German astronomer Johann Gottfried Galle, who found Neptune on the 23rd of September 1846 on his first night of searching, the first planet found by maths. On the 10th of October 1846, British astronomer William Lassell spotted Triton.
